general.name: ATM Skimming
general.description: Criminals attach devices to ATMs to steal card data. Always use ATMs inside banks, cover your PIN, and check for loose card slots.

general.name: Fake WiFi Networks
general.description: Scammers create WiFi hotspots with names similar to hotels/cafes to intercept your data. Use VPN and verify network names with staff.

general.name: Pickpocketing
general.description: Thieves work in groups to distract and steal. Keep valuables in front pockets, use money belts, stay alert in crowds.

general.name: Taxi Overcharging
general.description: Drivers take longer routes or tamper with meters. Use ride-sharing apps, agree on price beforehand, or insist on meter.

general.name: Currency Exchange Scams
general.description: Poor exchange rates or 'commission-free' exchanges that hide fees. Use banks or reputable exchange offices, check rates beforehand.

general.name: Fake Police
general.description: Scammers pose as police demanding to see your wallet/documents. Real police won't ask to check your wallet. Ask for ID and go to a police station.

general.name: Distraction Theft
general.description: Someone spills something on you, asks for directions, or creates a scene while an accomplice steals from you. Stay alert and secure belongings.

general.name: Restaurant Bill Padding
general.description: Extra charges added to bills for items not ordered. Always check your bill carefully and keep menus with prices.

scams.name: Taxi Meter Scams
scams.description: Taxis with rigged meters or drivers who claim the meter is broken. Use Uber/DiDi or agree on price before getting in. At airports, use official taxi booths only.

scams.name: Timeshare Presentations
scams.description: Aggressive salespeople offer 'free' tours, gifts, or discounts in exchange for attending a presentation. Very high-pressure sales tactics follow.

scams.name: Fake Police Bribes
scams.description: Fake or corrupt police demand bribes for fabricated violations. Ask for badge numbers, say you'll pay at the station, or ask to call your embassy.

scams.name: ATM Theft
scams.description: ATM skimming is common. Use ATMs inside banks during business hours. Cover your PIN and be wary of strangers offering 'help'.

scams.name: Overpriced Handicrafts
scams.description: Tourist markets often have inflated prices. Bargain firmly - starting at 50% of asking price is acceptable. Compare prices at multiple stalls.

scams.name: Water Scams
scams.description: Ensure bottled water seals are intact. Some vendors refill bottles with tap water. Buy from convenience stores.

tips: Use official taxi booths at airports
Don't flash expensive jewelry or electronics

scams.name: Tuk-Tuk Commission Scams
scams.description: Drivers offer cheap rides then take you to gem shops, tailors, or other stores where they earn commission. Politely decline detours.

scams.name: Jet Ski Damage Scams
scams.description: Renters claim you damaged the jet ski and demand huge payments. Take photos/video before renting. Use reputable companies or skip jet skis entirely.

scams.name: Temple/Palace 'Closed' Scam
scams.description: Strangers near attractions say it's closed and offer alternative tours. Verify at the entrance - these places rarely close unexpectedly.

scams.name: Gem Store Scams
scams.description: Locals claim there's a special government sale or once-a-year event. Gems are worthless or vastly overpriced. Never buy gems from tour referrals.

scams.name: Ping Pong Show Overcharging
scams.description: Touts promise low prices then present outrageous bills with threats. Avoid these establishments entirely.

scams.name: Bird Seed Scam
scams.description: Someone puts bird seed in your hand for 'free', then birds land on you and they demand payment for photos/cleaning.

scams.name: Fake Monks
scams.description: People dressed as monks ask for donations. Real monks don't solicit money on streets. Politely decline.

tips: Use Grab (ride-sharing app) instead of tuk-tuks
Never rent jet skis in Phuket
Verify attraction hours online before visiting
Keep calm - Thai culture values composure

scams.name: Pickpocketing (Barcelona)
scams.description: Barcelona has some of Europe's highest pickpocket rates, especially on Las Ramblas, in metro stations, and near Sagrada Familia.

scams.name: Petition Scam
scams.description: Someone asks you to sign a petition (often claiming to be deaf), then demands money or an accomplice picks your pocket while distracted.

scams.name: Three Card Monte
scams.description: Street gambling games are always rigged. 'Winners' are part of the scam to lure victims. Walking away is the only winning move.

scams.name: Flower/Rosemary Gift Scam
scams.description: Someone gives you a 'gift' flower or rosemary sprig (for 'luck'), then demands payment. Keep hands in pockets when approaching.

scams.name: Restaurant Overcharging
scams.description: Some tourist-area restaurants charge for bread, water, or have different prices for tourists. Check prices on menu before ordering.

scams.name: Soccer Ticket Scams
scams.description: Fake tickets for FC Barcelona or Real Madrid games. Only buy from official channels or authorized resellers.

tips: Don't put phones on restaurant tables
Be extra vigilant on La Rambla

scams.name: Gold Ring Scam
scams.description: Someone 'finds' a gold ring near you and offers to share it for cash. The ring is worthless brass. Walk away immediately.

scams.name: Friendship Bracelet Scam
scams.description: In Montmartre, men tie bracelets on your wrist claiming it's free, then demand payment. Keep hands in pockets, say 'Non' firmly.

scams.name: Petition Scam
scams.description: Common near Eiffel Tower and tourist areas. Groups distract you with clipboards while others pickpocket you.

scams.name: Fake Charity Workers
scams.description: People with official-looking badges collect 'donations' for fake charities. Never give cash to street collectors.

scams.name: Metro Pickpockets
scams.description: Teams work together on crowded metro cars and stations. Be especially alert when doors open/close.

scams.name: Cafe Receipt Swap
scams.description: Servers bring a bill for someone else's more expensive order. Always verify itemization matches what you ordered.

tips: Ignore anyone approaching with rings or bracelets
Book tours through official museum websites
Keep bags zipped and in front of you

scams.name: Gladiator Photo Scam
scams.description: People in Roman costumes pose for photos then demand large payments (€50+). Decline photos or agree on price first.

scams.name: Rose Sellers
scams.description: Sellers give flowers to women, then demand payment from their companions. Refuse to accept anything.

scams.name: Restaurant Scams
scams.description: Tourist-trap restaurants near attractions have hidden charges (coperto, service fees) and inflated prices. Walk a few blocks away for better value.

scams.name: Fake Designer Goods
scams.description: Street vendors sell counterfeit goods. Buying is illegal and can result in fines for tourists. Police conduct regular sweeps.

scams.name: Taxi Scams
scams.description: Rigged meters, scenic routes, or 'broken' meters. Use official taxi stands, insist on meter, or use apps like Free Now.

scams.name: Bracelet Scam
scams.description: Similar to France - string or bracelet forcibly tied to wrist with demands for payment. Keep moving, don't engage.

scams.name: Bird Poop Scam
scams.description: Someone squirts fake bird droppings on you, then an 'helpful' person cleans it while pickpocketing you. Decline help, go to bathroom.

tips: Eat where locals eat, away from monuments
Use official taxi stands at stations

scams.name: Ticket Touts
scams.description: Scalpers outside venues sell fake or overpriced tickets. Only buy from official box offices or authorized resellers.

scams.name: Shell Games
scams.description: Street gambling near tourist areas is always a scam. Apparent winners are accomplices. Never play.

scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Common in crowded areas like Oxford Street, tube stations, and markets. Use secure bags and stay alert.

scams.name: Minicab Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed minicabs charge excessive rates. Only use black cabs or pre-booked licensed minicabs/Uber.

scams.name: ATM Shoulder Surfing
scams.description: Criminals watch you enter PIN or distract you while stealing card. Use indoor ATMs, cover PIN, be aware of surroundings.

tips: Only use licensed black cabs or Uber
Keep bag zipped on public transport
Book theatre tickets from official sites
Be wary of 'helpful' strangers at ATMs

scams.name: Bar/Club Overcharging
scams.description: Rare but exists in areas like Kabukicho, Roppongi. Touts invite you to clubs with outrageous hidden fees. Avoid tout-promoted venues.

scams.name: Fake Monks
scams.description: People dressed as monks solicit donations aggressively. Real Japanese monks rarely solicit on streets. Politely decline.

scams.name: Photo Service Scams
scams.description: Someone offers to take your photo, then demands payment or runs off with your camera. Only ask obvious tourists or staff.

tips: Check prices before ordering at izakayas

scams.name: Taxi/Auto-Rickshaw Meters
scams.description: Drivers claim meters are broken or use rigged meters. Use Uber/Ola or agree on price beforehand. Know approximate distances.

scams.name: Hotel Commission Scam
scams.description: Drivers claim your hotel is closed/bad and take you to one paying them commission. Book directly and insist on your destination.

scams.name: Fake Government Tourist Office
scams.description: Scam offices near stations pose as official tourism bureaus selling overpriced tours. Only use verified government tourism offices.

scams.name: Gem/Carpet Scams
scams.description: Stories about reselling items at huge profit in your home country. These items are worthless or unsellable. Never buy to resell.

scams.name: Train Ticket Scams
scams.description: Touts say your train is cancelled or sell fake tickets. Book through official IRCTC website/app or at station counters.

scams.name: Short-Changing
scams.description: Vendors give wrong change quickly. Count your change carefully, especially with similar-colored notes.

scams.name: Free Tours Leading to Shops
scams.description: Friendly locals offer free city tours that end at high-pressure shops. Set clear boundaries or use verified guides.

tips: Book trains on official IRCTC only
Don't accept food/drinks from strangers on trains
Carry small denominations for exact change

scams.name: Motorbike Damage Scam
scams.description: Rental shops claim you damaged the bike and demand payment. Take detailed photos before renting. Use reputable shops.

scams.name: Cyclo Overcharging
scams.description: Cyclo drivers quote low prices then demand much more, claiming per person or per minute. Write down agreed total price.

scams.name: Shoe Cleaning Scam
scams.description: Someone squirts dirt on your shoes then offers to clean them for exorbitant fees. Decline firmly and walk away.

scams.name: Wrong Change
scams.description: Similar-looking notes are given as change. The 20,000 and 500,000 dong notes look similar. Check carefully.

scams.name: Fake Xe Om Apps
scams.description: Fake motorbike taxi drivers claim to be Grab drivers. Only get rides through the official app.

tips: Take photos of everything you rent
Agree on total prices in writing

scams.name: Pyramid Area Scams
scams.description: People offer 'free' camel rides, photos, or guides then demand huge payments. Agree on prices before anything, or decline.

scams.name: Perfume/Papyrus Shop Scams
scams.description: Tours include mandatory shopping stops with commission. Products are often overpriced or fake. Don't feel pressured to buy.

scams.name: Baksheesh Demands
scams.description: Everyone expects tips (baksheesh), but some demands are excessive. Carry small bills, tip appropriately (5-10 EGP for small services).

scams.name: Fake Antiques
scams.description: Vendors sell 'ancient' artifacts that are modern fakes. Real antiquities can't legally be sold. Assume everything is reproduction.

scams.name: Hotel/Restaurant Commission
scams.description: Taxi drivers get paid to take you to specific places. Insist on your chosen destination, use Uber/Careem.

tips: Use Uber or Careem for transport
Agree on all prices in advance
Be firm but polite when declining

scams.name: Shoe Shine Scam
scams.description: Someone drops a brush, you pick it up, they 'thank' you with a shoe shine then demand payment. Decline politely and walk away.

scams.name: Friendly Local Bar Scam
scams.description: New 'friends' invite you to a bar where women appear, drinks are ordered, and you get a massive bill. Only go to bars you chose.

scams.name: Carpet Shop Scams
scams.description: High-pressure sales in carpet shops, often combined with taxi kickbacks. Prices are highly inflated. Research and compare prices.

scams.name: Taxi Long Routes
scams.description: Drivers take circuitous routes, especially from airports. Use BiTaksi app, agree on price beforehand, or use metro.

scams.name: Grand Bazaar Overpricing
scams.description: Initial prices can be 5-10x the real value. Bargaining is expected. Start at 25-30% of asking price.

tips: Use BiTaksi or official taxi apps
Be skeptical of overly friendly strangers

scams.name: Express Kidnapping
scams.description: Criminals force victims to withdraw cash from ATMs. Use ATMs inside banks/malls during day. Don't resist if confronted.

scams.name: Fake Police
scams.description: Scammers pose as police demanding to check your wallet. Real police won't do this. Ask for ID and offer to go to a station.

scams.name: Distraction Theft
scams.description: Groups distract you (kids, spilled drinks) while accomplices steal. Keep valuables hidden and secure.

scams.name: Beach Theft
scams.description: Belongings stolen while swimming. Never leave valuables unattended. Use waterproof pouches for essentials.

scams.name: Taxi Meter Scams
scams.description: Rigged meters or scenic routes. Use 99 or Uber apps. From airports, use official taxi booths.

tips: Don't wear flashy jewelry or watches
Keep copies of documents, leave originals in safe

scams.name: False Guides
scams.description: People offer to guide you through medinas then demand payment or lead you to shops for commission. Hire official guides only.

scams.name: Closed Attraction Scam
scams.description: Someone says your destination is closed and offers alternatives. Verify yourself - places are rarely closed unexpectedly.

scams.name: Hennas Artists
scams.description: Women offer henna then demand high prices or give you black henna that can burn skin. Agree on price first, avoid black henna.

scams.name: Snake Charmers/Photo Scams
scams.description: Snakes placed on you, monkeys thrust at you for photos, then payment demanded. Keep distance, don't engage.

scams.name: Aggressive Bargaining
scams.description: Merchants may be very persistent. It's OK to walk away. Start bargaining at 20-30% of asking price.

scams.name: Currency Switch
scams.description: Merchants switch between dirhams and euros mid-negotiation. Always clarify currency and write down final price.

tips: Learn to say 'La shukran' (No thank you)

scams.name: Tea House Scam
scams.description: Friendly students invite you for tea/coffee, then you're presented with an enormous bill. Never accept invitations from strangers.

scams.name: Art Student Scam
scams.description: Students ask you to visit their 'exhibition' then pressure you to buy overpriced art. Politely decline invitations.

scams.name: Fake Monks
scams.description: People in monk robes solicit donations. Real monks don't beg. Decline and keep walking.

scams.name: Black Taxi Overcharging
scams.description: Unlicensed taxis charge much more than metered rates. Only use official taxis or DiDi app.

scams.name: Massage Parlor Scams
scams.description: Additional services charged without consent. Only use hotel-recommended or verified establishments.

tips: Be skeptical of overly friendly English speakers

scams.name: Restaurant Touts
scams.description: Aggressive restaurant staff in tourist areas lure you with promises, then overcharge. Walk further from main squares for better value.

scams.name: Taxi Scams
scams.description: Meters 'broken' or scenic routes taken. Insist on meter, use BEAT app, or agree on price first.

scams.name: Rental Vehicle Damage
scams.description: Claims of pre-existing damage on return. Take detailed photos of entire vehicle before leaving lot.

scams.name: ATM Charges
scams.description: ATMs may offer poor exchange rates with 'conversion services'. Always decline conversion and use your bank's rate.

scams.name: Drug Dealers (Lisbon)
scams.description: People in certain areas offer drugs that are actually bay leaves or other harmless substances. Decline and walk away.

scams.name: Pickpocketing
scams.description: Common in Lisbon's trams (especially Tram 28), Bairro Alto, and tourist areas. Keep valuables secure.

scams.name: Restaurant Appetizers
scams.description: Bread, olives, and snacks brought to table aren't free. Ask price or decline if you don't want them.

scams.name: Tuk-Tuk Overpricing
scams.description: Tuk-tuks in Lisbon can charge excessive rates. Agree on total price for entire tour beforehand.

tips: Use Bolt or Uber for transport
Carry bags in front in crowded areas

scams.name: Motorbike Rental Scams
scams.description: Similar to Vietnam - claims of damage, or bike 'stolen' while you have it. Use reputable shops, take extensive photos.

scams.name: Money Changer Scams
scams.description: Rigged calculators, sleight of hand, or distraction while counting. Use banks or ATMs instead.

scams.name: Fake Tour Operators
scams.description: Unlicensed operators with poor safety standards. Book diving, hiking, and tours through verified operators.

scams.name: Bali Taxi Mafia
scams.description: In some areas, app-based taxis are blocked. Official Blue Bird taxis are safe. Use apps where available.

scams.name: Temple Donation Scams
scams.description: Demands for large 'donations' at temples. Normal donation is 10,000-20,000 IDR. Don't feel pressured for more.

tips: Use Blue Bird taxis or Gojek/Grab
Get international driving permit for motorbikes
Book activities through hotels or Tripadvisor-reviewed operators

scams.name: Car Break-ins
scams.description: Valuables visible in parked cars invite break-ins. Never leave anything visible, use secure parking.

scams.name: ATM Scams
scams.description: Shoulder surfing, card trapping, or 'helpful' strangers. Use ATMs inside banks/malls, refuse all help.

scams.name: Township Tour Scams
scams.description: Unlicensed operators may be unsafe or exploitative. Book through reputable, community-supporting operators.

scams.name: Fake Police
scams.description: Criminals impersonate police. Ask for ID, offer to go to a station, call 10111 if suspicious.

scams.name: Smash and Grab
scams.description: At traffic lights, criminals smash windows to grab phones/bags. Keep valuables out of sight, windows up.

tips: Use Uber instead of metered taxis

scams.name: Rental Bond Scams
scams.description: Fake rental listings take deposits for non-existent properties. Verify properties exist before transferring money.

scams.name: Backpacker Job Scams
scams.description: Fake job ads take fees for non-existent farm work. Use verified job boards and never pay for job placements.

scams.name: SIM Card Overcharging
scams.description: Airport SIM card sellers may charge much more. Buy from Woolworths, Coles, or official carrier stores.

scams.name: Times Square Characters
scams.description: Costumed characters demand large tips for photos. Agree on price first or decline photos.

scams.name: CD/Mixtape Scam
scams.description: Someone gives you a 'free' CD then demands payment. Don't accept anything handed to you.

scams.name: Ticket Scalpers
scams.description: Fake or overpriced tickets outside venues. Use official ticket sources only.

scams.name: Petition Scams
scams.description: Similar to Europe - distraction technique for pickpockets or demanding donations. Decline and walk away.

scams.name: Fake WiFi
scams.description: Unsecured networks in airports/cafes can steal data. Use VPN, verify network names with staff.

tips: Be cautious in very touristy areas

scams.name: Orphanage Tourism
scams.description: Fake orphanages exploit children for donations. Never visit orphanages - it harms children. Support verified charities instead.

scams.name: Tuk-Tuk Commission Scams
scams.description: Drivers take you to shops/restaurants for commission. Be clear about destinations, don't accept detours.

scams.name: Milk/Rice Scam
scams.description: Children or women ask you to buy milk/rice from specific shops. Shop owners resell items after you leave. Give to verified charities.

scams.name: Fake Temple Fees
scams.description: People claim extra fees at Angkor Wat. Only official ticket counters charge fees. Show your pass if confronted.

scams.name: Money Exchange
scams.description: USD widely accepted but change may be in weak Cambodian riel. Know exchange rates, count your change.

tips: Buy Angkor pass from official counter only
Use PassApp or Grab for transport
